analysis: Reviewed ci.yml (head text only; no diff supplied, so the changed lines are unknown) and the release-swift.yml patch. release-swift.yml now takes the app bundle name, display name and executable names (APP_NAME, APP_DISPLAY_NAME, CLI_NAME, ENCLAVE_NAME, PRODUCT_*) from scripts/provider_release_identity.py, run as `python3 ... "$VERSION" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"` (hunks near lines 354 and 1213). The script is not visible, so its output is unverified. GITHUB_ENV writes are an injection sink if the script does not strictly validate VERSION and the JSON-derived names. In the first job the Resolve step runs before 'Validate release version integrity'. The global CLI_NAME and ENCLAVE_NAME env were removed. The hunk at ~line 235 now uses PRODUCT_CLI_NAME, and I could not confirm it is defined in that job. This would at worst be a build break, not a security issue. Flat bin/ names stay the SwiftPM product names, so coordinator registration and hash computation are unchanged. The final archive still checks stapling, Gatekeeper acceptance, `codesign --verify` with the fan-helper requirement, and the full CDHash extraction. The new smoke check `cli=${CLI_NAME}` depends on a source change outside the shown units. The bundle ID and signing identity are shared between dev and production (finding at line 15; T-054, T-055, T-053). ci.yml (units :4, :5): the permissions are contents: read, the actions are pinned by SHA, and no pull_request_target or secrets are used. The cache keys and workflow structure show no security-relevant change. A follow-up pass should check provider_release_identity.py input validation, whether the PRODUCT_* env is set in every job that uses it, and the dev/prod qualification separation on the platform side.

findings.detail: The new comment states that a dev release is packaged with a different app name and executable name, while the bundle identifier and the Developer ID signing identity stay the same as production. The dev app is meant to install beside the production app. Same-bundle-ID builds share the Keychain access group, the App Attest app identity and, plausibly, the SE key label and provider token storage (A-002, A-008, A-015). Separation then depends entirely on the coordinator qualifying the full CodeDirectory (T-054). It also depends on credential continuity not being read as machine identity (T-055). The threat model does not describe a dev channel, or whether a dev build may use or overwrite production credentials or tokens on the same Mac. Fix: document the dev channel in TB-011 and T-054/T-055, or give dev builds a distinct bundle ID, keychain group and key labels. Also confirm that the coordinator never qualifies dev CodeDirectory hashes for production serving.
findings.title: Dev release channel shares bundle ID and signing identity with production, but the threat model has no coverage
